scenario.title: 當主人和當客人的英文
scenario.context: 招待客人時，英文會大量使用祈使句：「請進」「隨便坐」「自己拿」。祈使句本來很直接，但搭配 Please / Feel free to / Help yourself，反而是最熱情、最有禮貌的招待方式。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Hey, come on in! Make yourself at home.

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Thanks for having me. I brought some dumplings for the potluck.
lines.zh: 謝謝邀請。我帶了一些水餃來百樂餐。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Amazing! Just put them on the table over there. Help yourself to drinks.
lines.zh: 太棒了！放那邊桌上就好。飲料自己拿。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Should I take my shoes off?

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Yes, please. There are slippers by the door.

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Your place is so cozy. I love the plants.
lines.zh: 你家好溫馨，我好喜歡那些植物。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Thanks! Feel free to look around. Don't mind the mess in the bedroom.
lines.zh: 謝謝！隨便看看。別管臥室的亂。

dialogues.title: At the end of the night

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Oh no, it's past midnight. I've missed the last MRT.
lines.zh: 糟了，已經過半夜了，我錯過末班捷運了。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Don't worry about it. Just crash here tonight.

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Are you sure? I don't want to overstay my welcome.
lines.zh: 你確定嗎？我不想打擾太久。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Don't be silly. The couch is super comfy. Let me grab you a blanket.
lines.zh: 別傻了，沙發超舒服，我去幫你拿條毯子。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: You're the best. Let me at least help clean up.
lines.zh: 你最好了。至少讓我幫忙收拾。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Leave the dishes. We'll do them in the morning.
lines.zh: 碗盤先放著，我們早上再洗。

patterns.en: Can I get you something to drink?
Should I take my shoes off?

chinglish.right: Please, have a seat. / Make yourself comfortable.
chinglish.why: 中文連說「坐坐坐」很熱情，英文重複祈使句聽起來像命令。

chinglish.wrong: You don't need to be polite.
chinglish.right: Make yourself at home. / Help yourself.
chinglish.why: 「別客氣」直翻 don't be polite 聽起來很怪，像叫對方沒禮貌。

chinglish.right: Please, have some more! There's plenty.
chinglish.why: 一直叫人多吃在英文文化裡可能讓人壓力很大。

chinglish.wrong: Sorry to disturb you.（到別人家時）
chinglish.why: 台灣人習慣說「打擾了」，英文用感謝取代道歉更自然。

grammar.title: 祈使句與客氣用語
grammar.oneLiner: 招待客人時，祈使句（Come in / Sit down / Help yourself）加上 please 或 feel free to，是最熱情自然的說法。
whenToUse: 邀請式祈使句：Come in! / Make yourself at home. / Have a seat.
help yourself (to…)：自己拿、自己來。Help yourself to snacks.
feel free to + V：隨意做。Feel free to look around.
否定祈使句：Don't worry. / Don't be silly.（安慰、客氣時很自然）
Let me + V：我來。Let me grab you a blanket.
語氣關鍵：語調友善、加上笑容，祈使句就是好客，不是命令。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 台灣人學英文時常聽到「祈使句不禮貌」，所以招待客人時會過度使用 Could you…? / Would you like to…?，反而顯得生疏。其實在熱情的情境下（邀請、給東西、安慰），英文母語者大量使用祈使句。關鍵在於：你是在給對方好處，還是在要求對方做事？

examples.correct: Come in, come in! Make yourself at home.
Help yourself to anything in the fridge.
examples.incorrect: Please help you to take food.

examples.correct: Feel free to use the Wi-Fi. The password's on the fridge.

Please make yourselves at home while I finish cooking.
examples.zh: 我煮完之前大家請隨意。

I'm so tired. I'm going to crash.

slang.meaning: 百樂餐（每人帶一道菜的聚會）

examples.en: We're having a potluck on Saturday. Can you bring a salad?
examples.zh: 我們週六辦百樂餐，你可以帶沙拉嗎？

examples.en: Potlucks are great because everyone tries new food.
examples.zh: 百樂餐很棒，大家都能吃到新東西。

slang.usage: 待得比主人希望的還久。

risk.note: 常用來客氣地表示自己要離開。

examples.en: I don't want to overstay my welcome. I'll head out soon.
examples.zh: 我不想打擾太久，我等下就走。

examples.en: Three weeks at his cousin's place? He's definitely overstayed his welcome.
examples.zh: 在他表哥家住三週？他絕對待太久了。
